comparison: Both evaluate the classifier methodology (C3, C14-C20). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with appropriate validation despite lower tremor performance (54%). Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, calling the classifier 'this paper's weak point' with 'limited efficacy' for tremor, though they acknowledge the interpretable parameters provide 'a reasonable starting point.'

Both address ataxia model findings (C21-C27). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical validation. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, with one specifically noting 'some of the interpretation of this work remains unclear to this reviewer (in particular Fig. 2, with ataxia models)' despite not challenging data quality.

Both evaluate dystonia model comparisons (C28-C35). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting compelling correlation between signature proportion and severity. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with no concerns raised and positive reception of electrophysiological findings demonstrating 'distinct changes in firing properties.'

Both assess propranolol pharmacological manipulation (C36-C40). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the shift in signatures provides pharmacological validation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, highlighting 'recordings across multiple phenotypic models including genetic and pharmacologic manipulations' as a major strength.

Both evaluate optogenetic experiments. OpenEval R7 covers behavioral validation (C45-C54) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R5 covers both electrophysiology (C41-C44) and behavior (C45-C54) plus overarching claim C5, all rated SUPPORTED. Reviewers strongly endorse findings as 'quite convincing' that specific patterns cause specific movement abnormalities.

OpenEval R6 addresses electrophysiological aspects of optogenetics (C41-C44) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R5 encompasses these claims within broader optogenetic evaluation (C5, C41-C54) also rated SUPPORTED. Both affirm that same neurons produce different signatures with different stimulation patterns.

OpenEval R9 evaluates overarching conclusion C5 about spike signatures being sufficient for disease phenotypes, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes C5 within comprehensive optogenetic evaluation (C5, C41-C54), also rated SUPPORTED with strong reviewer endorsement of causal demonstration.

Both address main conclusions. OpenEval R10 covers C6 and C73 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R6 covers C6, C65, C66 rated SUPPORTED. Both affirm the central conclusion that specific cerebellar output patterns are sufficient to cause specific movement abnormalities, with reviewers calling findings 'quite convincing.'

OpenEval R19 evaluates synthesis claims C65-C66 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes these claims (C6, C65, C66) also rated SUPPORTED. Both affirm electrophysiological differences are well-documented and optogenetic experiments provide strong causal evidence.

OpenEval R8 evaluates overarching conclusion C4 about phenotypically similar models sharing spike signatures, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 addresses related ataxia findings (C4, C21-C27) but rates UNCERTAIN due to interpretation challenges with Fig. 2 data.

OpenEval R1 evaluates foundational background claims C1-C2 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 covers broader background (C1-C2, C7-C13) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept these as well-established premises without challenge.

OpenEval R11 evaluates historical literature citations C7-C9 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims within broader background evaluation (C1-C2, C7-C13) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept clinical context as well-established.

OpenEval R12 evaluates prior work establishing archetypal models C10-C13 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims in background evaluation (C1-C2, C7-C13) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept these as appropriate foundation.

OpenEval R14 evaluates claims C56-C57 about functional vs structural changes rated SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes these claims within broader mechanistic interpretations (C56-C60, C73) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept that optogenetic experiments demonstrate pathological signatures can arise from functional changes.

OpenEval R15 evaluates speculative claims C58-C59 about comorbidity and transient symptoms rated UNCERTAIN. Peer R7 includes these claims within mechanistic interpretations (C56-C60, C73) rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval more cautious, noting these require additional validation.

OpenEval R16 evaluates therapeutic recommendations C60, C67 rated UNCERTAIN as speculative. Peer R7 includes C60 within mechanistic interpretations (C56-C60, C73) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes C67 in methodological conclusions also rated SUPPORTED. Reviewers accept as reasonable extensions.

OpenEval R16 evaluates therapeutic claim C67 rated UNCERTAIN. Peer R8 includes C67 with methodological conclusions (C64, C67) rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clinical validation required; peer reviewers accept as reasonable translational conclusion.

Both address technical limitations. OpenEval R17 evaluates C61-C62 rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging inability to definitively identify recorded cell types. Peer R11 covers C61-C63 rated SUPPORTED, with reviewers calling work 'technically impressive' without raising concerns.

OpenEval R18 evaluates methodological claims C63-C64 rated SUPPORTED. Peer R11 includes C63 within technical methodology (C61-C63) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept the recording approach despite acknowledged limitations.

OpenEval R18 evaluates C64 about population-level recordings rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes C64 with translational conclusions (C64, C67) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept that classifier approach can identify disease signatures despite limitations.

OpenEval R13 evaluates interpretation C55 about degenerative models rated SUPPORTED. Peer R9 includes C55 within mechanistic interpretations (C55, C68-C72) also rated SUPPORTED. Both accept as reasonable interpretation with appropriate caution.

OpenEval R20 evaluates mechanistic interpretations C68-C70 rated UNCERTAIN as speculative. Peer R9 includes these claims (C55, C68-C72) rated SUPPORTED. Reviewers accept as reasonable hypotheses; OpenEval more cautious about requiring additional validation.

OpenEval R21 evaluates C71-C72 rated SUPPORTED, with C71 supported by proportional data and C72 acknowledging optogenetic caveat. Peer R9 includes these claims (C55, C68-C72) rated SUPPORTED. Both accept interpretations as reasonable.
